explanation: The August 9, 2011 document contains a highly substantive forward guidance shift: the Committee replaced the open-ended 'extended period' language with an explicit calendar-based commitment to keep the federal funds rate exceptionally low 'at least through mid-[masked year],' a concrete and unprecedented time-contingent pledge that represented a major dovish regime change. Additionally, the statement acknowledged that downside risks to the economic outlook had 'increased,' that growth had been 'considerably slower than expected,' and explicitly flagged discussion of the full range of policy tools including balance sheet adjustments, strongly signaling openness to further QE — all of which would plausibly cause a structural break in financial market data.
